topic: bro_wait ignores timeout_seconds: bounded wait blocks far past its timeout against a running task
notes:
BUG (observed in live session 2026-05-28): bro_wait called with timeout_seconds=240 against a running codex bro (task df798de0) did NOT return after 240s. It blocked ~40 min (full wall-clock from dispatch) until the operator manually interrupted. A bounded wait that does not honor its bound.

Evidence / what's already verified (so the next agent doesn't re-walk it):
- Param OK: WaitParams.timeout_seconds: Option<f64> with #[serde(default)] (src/tools/bro_params.rs:248). Caller passed 240 -> Some(240.0).
- Handler OK on static read: bro_wait passes p.timeout_seconds straight to orch::wait_for_task_with_timeout (src/tools/dispatch.rs:884-928, call at :905), then returns task_result_json on completed / timeout_snapshot_json on timeout.
- Timeout fn correct IN ISOLATION and unit-tested: wait_for_task_with_timeout (src/orchestration/mod.rs:1827) wraps wait_for_task in tokio::time::timeout; test_wait_for_task_timeout (mod.rs:2904) asserts it returns false after 0.1s for a Running task.
- So the three obvious layers are individually correct, yet the real invocation did not honor the bound => genuine latent defect, NOT caller misuse.

Anomaly worth noting: even if timeout had been None, wait_for_task should have returned when the task completed (~T0+6min; status elapsed was 5m46s, report posted ~34m before the eventual status check, summing to ~40min). So neither Some(240) nor None explains a 40-min block. The wait future appears to have stopped being driven at all.

Leading hypothesis (UNCONFIRMED — do not treat as root cause): wait_for_task (mod.rs:1806) acquires a synchronous parking_lot lock task.inner.lock() inside its async poll. tokio::time::timeout cannot cancel a future blocked INSIDE poll() (only at await points). If inner.lock() is contended/held during a long streaming run, the worker thread blocks inside poll() and both the 240s timer and the completion notify are defeated. BUT all inner.lock() sites I inspected are short-lived clones, so this does not obviously explain a 40-min hang. Needs a real repro.

Suggested next step: reproduce deterministically — fire bro_wait with a short timeout against a known long-running task and confirm whether the timeout fires; add tracing around wait_for_task_with_timeout entry/exit and the inner.lock sites; consider whether the rmcp request future / runtime driving the tool handler is the actual culprit rather than wait_for_task itself. Fix from evidence; do not ship a speculative patch.

Related (do not conflate): thread-1bab9018 covers bro usage reporting (cached_input_tokens) — separate concern.
